exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise that works the chest, shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body is in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push back up until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: Squat
exercises.description: A lower-body exercise that works the quads, glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Keep your chest up and push your hips back as you bend your knees.
Lower until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor, or as far as is comfortable.
Push through your heels to stand back up.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: A core exercise that builds stability through the abs, back and shoulders.
instructions: Rest on your forearms with your elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Hold the position without letting your hips sag or lift.
Lower your knees to the floor to rest.
exercises.safety: Keep your hips level and your neck in line with your spine. If your lower back starts to ache, drop to your knees or rest.

exercises.name: Stand on One Foot
exercises.description: A simple balance exercise where you hold yourself steady on one leg. It helps build the steadiness you need for everyday movements like walking and climbing stairs.
equipment: Optional: a wall or sturdy chair for support. This modification is for seniors, people with injuries, or anyone who needs help balancing.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet together. If you're using support, face a wall with your arms outstretched and your fingertips touching it, or hold the back of a sturdy chair.
Lift your left foot off the floor, keeping your hips level and a slight bend in your standing knee.
Hold for 5 to 10 seconds, then gently place your foot back on the floor.
Repeat with your right leg. Do 3 lifts on each side.
exercises.safety: Clear the space around you and keep a wall or sturdy chair within reach in case you lose your balance. Stop and rest if you feel dizzy or unsteady.

pathways.name: Beginner Strength
pathways.description: A two-week introduction to bodyweight strength training, alternating upper- and lower-body days with rest in between.
